page: Amazon Web Services m6id.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors, delivering 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with a 3.5 GHz clock speed. The system features 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled directly with 7,600 GB of local NVMe SSD instance store capacity, and the network interface supports a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. While single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the average category, multi-core execution is strong, placing in the top 25 percent of tested systems. The server demonstrates top-tier performance in Passmark CPU tests, extended instructions, and cryptographic operations, ranking in the top 10 percent. Memory bandwidth is also strong, with uncached read speeds reaching 339.2 GB/sec and write speeds at 133.21 GB/sec.

This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded workloads, database operations, and large-scale web serving. The 7,600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage supports high-throughput data access, reflected in strong database operations and Redis SET benchmarks. However, single-threaded tasks and large LLM text generation tasks show average performance, indicating that workloads requiring high single-core frequency or GPU acceleration may face limitations on this architecture.
